lede: This week: a Kiyoshi Kurosawa deep cut on Criterion, a Taiwanese crime-comedy and Turkish thriller sliding onto Netflix, Guy Ritchie's MobLand back for round two, and an announced slate topped by Lee Chang-dong's long-awaited Possible Love.

shortlist.title: Youth
shortlist.meta: Creator/star Sharon Horgan; with Sharlene Whyte, Rupert Friend. New comedy series.
shortlist.blurb: A newly divorced 50-year-old juggles dating, an ailing parent, and her almost-grown son in Sharon Horgan's latest sharp, wickedly funny dramedy.

shortlist.title: Call My Agent! The Movie
shortlist.meta: Dir. Émilie Noblet; with Camille Cottin, Laure Calamy. 120 min.
shortlist.blurb: Five years after the ASK talent agency closed, director-to-be Andréa scrambles to reassemble her old agent squad when her lead actor bails days before shooting.

shortlist.title: Penance
shortlist.meta: Dir. Kiyoshi Kurosawa. Five-part psychological thriller presented as a feature.
shortlist.blurb: Four women who witnessed a childhood friend's murder are told by the grieving mother they must identify the killer — or perform whatever "penance" she demands.

shortlist.title: The Fixers
shortlist.meta: Dir. Hung Tzu-hsuan & Henri Chang; with Christopher Lee, Shou Lou. Season 1, 8 episodes.
shortlist.blurb: A debt-ridden gangster stumbles into a secret temple-based fixer organization solving problems for criminals and politicians alike in this Taiwanese action-comedy.

shortlist.title: MobLand
shortlist.meta: Creator/dir. Guy Ritchie; with Tom Hardy, Pierce Brosnan, Helen Mirren. Season 2, weekly.
shortlist.blurb: The Harrigan crime family fractures from within as rival gangs circle in Guy Ritchie's slick, starry crime saga — already renewed for season 3.

shortlist.title: Not a Stranger
shortlist.meta: With Elçin Sangu, Ozan Dolunay, Melis Sezen. Season 1, 8 episodes.
shortlist.blurb: A painter finally finds the perfect nanny for her child — except the nanny is deeply, unsettlingly wrong — in this slow-burn Turkish domestic thriller.

movies.title: It Ends
movies.blurb: An $80K SXSW breakout about grads trapped in an endless two-lane-road cosmic-horror loop — currently sitting at 100% on Rotten Tomatoes.

movies.title: Best of the Best
movies.blurb: Two childhood best friends discover UCLA's Bollywood-fusion dance team is more cutthroat than expected in this crowd-pleasing Netflix comedy.

tv.title: The Paper
tv.blurb: Season 2 of the Office-verse mockumentary follows Ned Sampson chasing a story that could sink the Toledo Truth Teller.

tv.title: Slow Horses
tv.blurb: The Slough House misfits are hunted and forced on the run in what critics are calling the show's best season yet (100% RT).

tv.title: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story
tv.blurb: Ryan Murphy's anthology tackles Lizzie Borden with Ella Beatty in the lead, though critics have called it thin ("faux-feminist nonsense," per THR).

tv.title: The Traitors: New Blood
tv.blurb: An all-civilian cast of 22 competes for $250K in this celebrity-free spinoff of the hit competition format.

tv.title: Neagley
tv.blurb: Reacher's first spinoff centers on Frances Neagley's own detective work and became Prime's #2 global show within a day.

tv.title: Colin From Accounts
tv.blurb: The beloved Australian rom-com signs off with a warm, low-key finale finally answering whether Ashley and Gordon were meant to be.

tv.title: Golden Axe
tv.blurb: A SEGA arcade adaptation buried by weak marketing turns out to be a stylish, genuinely funny animated surprise.

tv.title: Route 187
tv.blurb: Tyler Perry's limited series follows a journalist investigating a bus route nicknamed for the police homicide code.

tv.title: The Scandal
tv.blurb: Son Ye-jin and Ji Chang-wook headline this lavish Joseon-set adaptation of Dangerous Liaisons.

tv.title: Made in Korea
tv.blurb: Hyun Bin's KCIA thriller wraps its final season as old rivals settle the score nine years later.

tv.title: Plastic Beauty
tv.blurb: A surgeon ousted from her hospital clashes with a celebrity cosmetic-surgery clinic's star doctor in this sharp Japanese drama.

tv.title: Stranger Things: Tales from '85
tv.blurb: The animated Stranger Things spinoff sends the Hawkins Investigators Club chasing a ghostly, flower-obsessed creature in a 1985 Valentine's arc.

anime.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba
anime.blurb: All four seasons plus the Mugen Train film land on a new streaming home for the first time — an easy miss since it's not a new episode, just a new place to watch.

anime.title: The End of Evangelion
anime.blurb: Hideaki Anno's genre-redefining mecha classic and its series join Criterion's library — a striking curatorial statement from a channel not known for anime.

catalog.title: Romería
catalog.blurb: Carla Simón's autobiographical Cannes drama follows an orphaned aspiring filmmaker investigating her late parents' mysterious deaths.

catalog.title: Our Land
catalog.blurb: Legendary Argentine auteur Lucrecia Martel's documentary debut investigates the murder of an indigenous land-rights leader.

catalog.title: The Love Witch
catalog.blurb: Anna Biller's cult feminist horror-comedy, shot on lush 35mm in a deliberately retro style, joins Criterion's library.

catalog.title: Cemetery Man
catalog.blurb: Rupert Everett battles the reanimated dead in this beloved Italian horror-comedy cult classic.

catalog.title: Marighella
catalog.blurb: Wagner Moura's directorial debut chronicles the militant who resisted Brazil's military dictatorship.

catalog.title: Linda Linda Linda
catalog.blurb: A freshly restored print of this beloved Japanese teen-band indie joins Criterion's "Girl Bands!" collection.

catalog.title: King of New York
catalog.blurb: Christopher Walken anchors this gritty Abel Ferrara crime classic, part of a full career retrospective now streaming.

announced.title: Possible Love
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed a Nov. 6 global streaming date for Lee Chang-dong's Venice Silver Lion winner, his first film in 8 years, days after its Oct. 23 theatrical bow.

announced.title: Pride and Prejudice
announced.blurb: Netflix set a Dec. 3 premiere and released first-look photos this week for Dolly Alderton's 6-part Austen adaptation starring Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden.

announced.title: Ink
announced.blurb: A new trailer confirmed Danny Boyle's Rupert Murdoch drama, which opened Venice, streams on Netflix Jan. 8 after a brief December theatrical run.

announced.title: East of Eden
announced.blurb: Netflix dropped the trailer confirming all 7 episodes of Zoe Kazan's Steinbeck reimagining, starring Florence Pugh, drop Oct. 1.

announced.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – Infinity Castle
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed via its official account that the highest-grossing anime film ever finally lands for US subscribers Sept. 28.

announced.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2
announced.blurb: A new trailer confirmed Trigger's standalone follow-up to the acclaimed anime hits Netflix Oct. 20.

announced.title: Below
announced.blurb: Netflix's trailer confirmed all 6 episodes of this Josh Hartnett sea-monster horror series, set in a Newfoundland fishing town, drop Oct. 8.

announced.title: War
announced.blurb: HBO/Sky released a trailer confirming Dominic West and Sienna Miller's 8-part legal drama premieres on Max Oct. 1.

announced.title: Sacrifice
announced.blurb: Netflix's trailer confirmed Romain Gavras's TIFF volcano-cult satire, starring Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy, streams Oct. 16.

announced.title: Disclosure Day
announced.blurb: Peacock confirmed a streaming date for Spielberg's alien-conspiracy thriller starring Emily Blunt, arriving Oct. 9 after its summer theatrical run.

announced.title: Blue Road
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed this Korean-Japanese cross-border serial-killer thriller, starring Son Suk Ku, lands in November (exact date TBD).

announced.title: The Apothecary Diaries
announced.blurb: Crunchyroll's fall lineup announcement confirmed the long-awaited third season returns Sept. 26.
